sheet-1-1.description: The lower half of sheet 1, below a heavy dividing line that separates it from the key map, street index and notes printed above. Drawn at 100 feet to an inch, it covers the southern end of Pompton Lakes between Ramapo Avenue in the west and the Ramapo River in the east, from the Mill Street area and the Paterson and Hamburg Turnpike in the north to Riverdale Road along the bottom edge. River View Road crosses the sheet in two stretches, an offset western one meeting Ramapo Avenue and an eastern one running from Lincoln Avenue to the turnpike, and Watervliet Avenue runs west from Ramapo Avenue. Lincoln, Van Ness and Mathes Avenues run south from River View Road. Most of the area is laid out in narrow house lots, many still vacant, with scattered frame dwellings and garages, several marked as drawn from plans, and lots east of Ramapo Avenue fronting streets marked not open. In the north the Rhinesmith Concrete Products Manufacturing Company works lies along Mill Street with its factory and warehouse buildings, and at the north-east corner beside the turnpike are an auto repair shop and the New Jersey State Police headquarters. A pond and a creek run south towards the Ramapo River, which bounds the sheet on the east with the borough limits and Wayne Township beyond it; the turnpike crosses the river on a steel bridge at the right edge. Water pipes of four and six inches and hydrants are shown along the streets. Block numbers 87 to 95, with suffixes, are printed in the blocks, and dwellings are noted as continuing beyond Riverdale Road.
notes: River View Road is Riverview Road in OpenStreetMap; it is drawn in two offset stretches, west of Ramapo Avenue and from Lincoln Avenue east.
Mill is printed without a suffix; the index and OpenStreetMap give Mill Street, marked not open east of the concrete works.
Rhinesmith Concrete Products Mfg. Co. (power electric, no lights or heat) and the N.J. State Police Headquarters.

Scale 100 ft (map part); upper half is the key map (1600 ft to an inch), water/fire notes and street index, left out of the mask. Main part: Ramapo Av, Lincoln Av, Van Ness Av, Mathes Av, River View Rd, Watervliet Av, Riverdale Rd, Mill St, Paterson & Hamburg Tpke; Rhinesmith Concrete Products. Part 2: inset lower right, Jersey Central Power & Light Co hydro-electric plant on the Ramapo River at the Paterson & Hamburg Tpke steel bridge. Part 2 continues the main map east of its right edge (same scale and orientation); placed from points carried from the steel bridge on part 1.

sheet-1-2.description: A small inset in the lower right corner of sheet 1, boxed off by a heavy line and drawn at the same scale of 100 feet to an inch and with north up. It continues the main map of the sheet east of its right edge, at the point where the Paterson and Hamburg Turnpike crosses the Ramapo River on a steel bridge about 50 feet wide. The turnpike comes in from the north-west, 70 feet wide, with a six inch water pipe and a hydrant, and a 30 foot road leaves it to the east above the river. Between that road and the river, east of the bridge, stands the Pompton Lakes hydro-electric plant of the Jersey Central Power and Light Company, a fireproof building of concrete floors and roof and brick walls built in 1919, noted as having men on duty day and night and steam heat. The Ramapo River runs across the lower half of the inset, with the borough limits line along its centre and Wayne Township to the south. The inset adds little beyond the plant itself; the bridge and the river banks it draws are the same as those at the right edge of the main map, which is how the inset was placed.
notes: Jersey Central Power & Light Co. Pompton Lakes Hydro-Electric Plant, built 1919.
Placed from three points carried from the steel bridge drawn on sheet 1 part 1; no street junction is drawn in the inset.

Scale 100 ft (map part); upper half is the key map (1600 ft to an inch), water/fire notes and street index, left out of the mask. Main part: Ramapo Av, Lincoln Av, Van Ness Av, Mathes Av, River View Rd, Watervliet Av, Riverdale Rd, Mill St, Paterson & Hamburg Tpke; Rhinesmith Concrete Products. Part 2: inset lower right, Jersey Central Power & Light Co hydro-electric plant on the Ramapo River at the Paterson & Hamburg Tpke steel bridge. Part 2 continues the main map east of its right edge (same scale and orientation); placed from points carried from the steel bridge on part 1.

sheet-2.description: Sheet 2 shows the northern end of the Wanaque Avenue business district in Pompton Lakes, drawn at 50 feet to an inch. Wanaque Avenue enters from the lower left, runs north past the main shopping block and bends to the north-west to cross the Wanaque River on a bridge at the upper left, where the river sweeps in a wide curve down the left side of the sheet. Colfax Avenue meets Wanaque Avenue near the foot of the sheet and runs east to its junction with Lakeside Avenue, which runs north from Colfax Avenue to the railroad and, as a curved street, south-east towards the bottom right corner. The N.Y.S. & W. R.R. crosses the sheet from lower left to upper right with its sidings and the Pompton Lakes passenger station on the south side, and Cannon Ball Road follows the track on the north side towards the right edge. Wanaque Avenue is lined with stores and offices in brick and concrete block, among them the post office, an office building, the 1st National Bank, a large drug store block, hardware and paints, the Pompton House hotel and an auto repairing shop. East of Lakeside Avenue are the yards and sheds of the Pompton Lakes Building Supply Co., with lumber storage, car sheds, cement storage, a silk mill with its own power plant, and a large garage for 25 cars near the lower right. The upper part of the sheet is mostly open land with a few dwellings and one large building at the upper right. Block numbers 25, 30, 31, 31A, 62 and 63 are printed, and the adjoining sheets 3, 4 and 8 are named in the margins.
notes: Cannon Ball Road is Cannonball Road in OpenStreetMap.
The curved street running south-east from Colfax Avenue is also lettered Lakeside Avenue.
The N.Y.S. & W. R.R. is the Southern Division Main Line in OpenStreetMap.
Scale 50 ft. Downtown north: Wanaque Av, Cannon Ball Rd, Colfax Av, Lakeside Av, Pompton Av; railroad (N.Y.S.& W.) crossing; Wanaque River at left.

sheet-3.description: Sheet 3 covers the centre of Pompton Lakes along Wanaque Avenue, from the Lakeside Avenue corner at the top to Pompton Avenue at the bottom, drawn at 50 feet to an inch. Wanaque Avenue runs diagonally down the sheet with the Wanaque River along the left side and in the lower left. Lenox Avenue enters from the right edge and meets Wanaque Avenue about two thirds of the way down, and Pompton Avenue crosses the bottom edge. A short length of Lakeside Avenue appears at the top right. The frontage on both sides of Wanaque Avenue is the town's main street: stores, a department store, a drug store, a bakery, the Colonial Hotel, auto supplies and a plumber, a bowling alley, a photographer, a motion picture theatre, an auto repair shop with show room, the Fire Department with a fire alarm box, and the printing office of The Bulletin newspaper. On the east side stand the Municipal Building with jail and police rooms and, at the right edge, Pompton Lakes School, a large brick building with an auditorium court. The Einstein Memorial Library, a pink brick building, stands at the lower right between Wanaque Avenue and Pompton Avenue. Between and behind these are detached frame dwellings with garages on large lots, and a good deal of vacant land. The Wanaque River is lettered along the lower left. Block numbers 26, 30, 63 and 70 are printed, and sheets 2, 5, 6 and 8 are named in the margins.
notes: The sheet is cut at Lakeside Avenue at the top; the rest of that street is on sheets 2 and 4.
Einstein Memorial Library is lettered on the sheet.
Scale 50 ft. Downtown: Wanaque Av, Pompton Av, Lakeside Av; Ramapo River along the left; municipal building, school.

sheet-4.description: Sheet 4 shows the lumber yard and the residential blocks to the north-east of the centre of Pompton Lakes, drawn at 50 feet to an inch. Across the upper left the N.Y.S. & W. R.R. runs from lower left to upper right with a fan of yard tracks, and Cannon Ball Road follows its north-west side. Colfax Avenue curves across the middle of the sheet from the left edge to the right, Lakeside Avenue runs along the bottom, and two streets cross between them, lettered Adrian near the left and Legion near the right; Romain Avenue runs down the right side, and Ramapo Avenue is lettered below Lakeside Avenue at the foot of the sheet. In the upper left are the yards of the Pompton Lakes Coal, Feed & Lumber Co., with a 2-storey lumber shed, shingle storage, a coal pocket with conveyor, cement storage, a wagon shed and rows of cord wood piles, and the Progressive Cement Products Co., manufacturers of cement blocks, with a concrete block works. The remaining blocks are mostly detached frame dwellings and outbuildings, with a carpenter shop and a small blue building among them. A street in the northern blocks is lettered 'Not named', with 'From Plans' beside it. Block numbers 1, 31, 32, 32A, 61, 61A and 62 are printed, and sheets 2, 5, 9 and 10 are named in the margins.
notes: Adrian and Legion are lettered without a suffix here; sheet 5 letters them Adrian St. and Legion St. They are Adrian Street and Legion Street in OpenStreetMap.
Cannon Ball Road is Cannonball Road in OpenStreetMap.
Scale 50 ft. Cannon Ball Rd, Colfax Av, Lakeside Av, Lenox Av, Romain Av, Van Av; railroad across the top.

sheet-5.description: Sheet 5 covers the residential blocks south-east of the centre of Pompton Lakes, between Lakeside Avenue at the top and Pompton Avenue at the bottom, drawn at 50 feet to an inch. Ramapo Avenue runs down the middle of the sheet, tilting slightly to the right, Lenox Avenue crosses from the left edge to the middle, and Romain Avenue runs along the right edge. Adrian St. and Legion St. are lettered as stubs entering Lakeside Avenue from the north at the top. The area is almost entirely detached frame dwellings, many of two storeys, with their garages and sheds, set on long narrow lots. At the upper left stand the Pompton Lakes Community House, Inc. and the I.O.O.F. Hall, and at the lower left St. Mary's R.C. Church, heated by steam and lit by electricity, with a shed and a concrete block building near it. Part of the school building of sheet 3 appears at the left edge. Water pipes of four and six inches are shown in the streets, with hydrants and fire alarm boxes at several corners. Block numbers 63, 64, 69 and 70 are printed, with the old numbers in brackets, and sheets 3, 4, 6, 7 and 10 are named in the margins. A large part of the left centre is vacant.
notes: St. Mary's R.C. Church is lettered at the lower left.
Scale 50 ft. Lakeside Av, Lenox Av, Bartholf Av, Pompton Av, Ramapo Av, Lincoln Av.

sheet-6.description: Sheet 6 covers the west side of the centre of Pompton Lakes, where Wanaque Avenue divides into two ways, drawn at 50 feet to an inch. Wanaque Avenue enters at the top and runs south, with Pompton Avenue crossing at the top and Bartholf Avenue about a third of the way down. Near the bottom it splits: one branch curves west and becomes the Paterson and Hamburg Turnpike, which runs east to west across the lower part of the sheet and crosses a concrete bridge at the left edge, and the other branch curves east to Passaic Avenue. A triangular plot lettered Park lies between the branches. The Turnpike also runs south-east to the bottom right corner, where a street lettered Center meets it at the bottom edge. The Wanaque River occupies the upper left and left, with two islands and a wide bend, and is lettered across the top. Buildings are scattered: detached frame dwellings with outbuildings between Wanaque Avenue and the river, a frame auto repair shop of concrete block on the Turnpike near the left, and dwellings east of Wanaque Avenue in blocks 71 and 74. The lower middle of the sheet is open land (block 80). Water pipes of four and eight inches, a fire alarm box and hydrants are shown. Sheets 3, 5, 7 and 11 are named in the margins.
notes: Paterson & Hamburg Turnpike is Paterson-Hamburg Turnpike in OpenStreetMap; its modern line is displaced from the drawn one here and is not used for control.
Center is lettered without a suffix; it is Center Street in OpenStreetMap and Sheet 7 letters it Center St.
Scale 50 ft. Pompton Av, Bartholf Av, Passaic Av, Paterson & Hamburg Tpke; Ramapo River at top left.

sheet-7.description: Sheet 7 covers four residential blocks in the centre of Pompton Lakes, drawn at 50 feet to an inch. Pompton Avenue runs along the top edge of the sheet, cut at its centre line, and Bartholf Avenue and Passaic Avenue cross the sheet east to west. Ramapo Avenue runs north to south through the middle and Lincoln Avenue along the right edge, so the sheet shows the two rows of blocks between Ramapo Avenue and the area to the west, and between Ramapo and Lincoln Avenues. In the lower left corner the Paterson and Hamburg Turnpike crosses diagonally, with the end of Center Street meeting it at the bottom edge. The blocks are given over almost entirely to detached frame dwellings with their outbuildings and garages, set well back on large lots; several houses are brick veneered or have stone first stories, and a few small structures are drawn in brick. The one institutional building is Christ Church (Episcopal), a frame church on the south side of Passaic Avenue just west of Ramapo Avenue. Water pipes of four and six inches are shown in the streets, with hydrants at the corners and fire alarm boxes on Pompton and Passaic Avenues. Block numbers 71 to 76 and 84, with older numbers in brackets, are printed in the blocks. The large lots of the lower right block are subdivided into narrow house lots fronting Lincoln Avenue. The adjoining sheets are 5 to the north, 6 to the west, 10 to the east and 11 to the south, as printed in the margins.
notes: Paterson & Hamburg Turnpike is Paterson-Hamburg Turnpike in OpenStreetMap.
Christ Church (Episcopal) on Passaic Avenue.
Scale 50 ft. Pompton Av, Bartholf Av, Passaic Av, Ramapo Av, Lincoln Av, Center St, Paterson & Hamburg Tpke. Pilot sheet.

sheet-8.description: Sheet 8 covers Pompton Junction and the north-west side of Pompton Lakes, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north to the upper left. Montclair Avenue runs down the left edge to Broad, and Midland Avenue runs parallel to it, both crossed by Willard at the middle and by Broad near the bottom. Ringwood Avenue runs from the top, through the Willard junction where Wanaque Avenue branches east to the Wanaque River, and south to the bottom. East of Ringwood Avenue, the streets Laura, Ivy, Grove and Locust are laid out between it and the river. Hershfield, Kluge and Albert run east and west in the upper half, across the blocks numbered 12 to 17, several of them marked Not Open, with Twin Lake and Post Brook winding between them. In the upper right is the Artistic Weaving Co., a large factory with factory buildings, a power plant and smaller works on the shore of Lake Inez, and the Dupont Fuse Works lies beyond to the north (admittance refused). Other buildings include the Public Service Distribution Building at the left edge, a filling station, auto show rooms and repair shops at Willard and Ringwood, The Old Homestead (boarding), Federal Rock Manor with its inn, St. Paul's Home for Aged, a boarding house called Mansion Ho., and the Pompton Junction R.R. station at the lower left. The N.Y.S. & W. R.R. crosses the lower right, with the Wanaque River.
notes: The printed north arrow points about 12 degrees left of up; the fitted rotation of the sheet is about 6 degrees.

Hershfield, Kluge, Albert, Willard, Broad, Locust, Laura, Ivy and Grove are Hershfield Street, Kluge Street, Albert Street, Willard Street, Broad Street, Locust Street, Laura Street, Ivy Street and Grove Street in OpenStreetMap.
Concrete bridges carry Broad over Post Brook.
Blocks west of Midland Avenue marked Not Open are not used for control; Hershfield and Kluge streets there are not drawn as open streets.
A dam is lettered across the lower end of Twin Lake.

Scale 100 ft, north about 15 degrees left of up. Pompton Junction area: Montclair Av, Midland Av, Willard, Ringwood Av, Wanaque Av, Broad, Locust, Laura, Ivy, Grove, Hershfield, Kluge, Albert; Twin Lake, Post Brook; Artistic Weaving Co; N.Y.S.& W. R.R.; Wanaque River.

sheet-9.description: Sheet 9 is drawn at 100 feet to an inch and turned on the page, with north pointing to the left (about 60 degrees anticlockwise from up in the fit). It covers the north-eastern residential district of Pompton Lakes between the New York, Susquehanna and Western Railroad, whose tracks run down the left edge with Crandall Street and Circle Avenue beyond them, and Pompton Lake on the right. Colfax Avenue runs down the sheet left of centre, crossed at the top by Schuyler Avenue and by Grant Avenue, which runs diagonally to the upper right. Between Colfax Avenue and Lakeside Avenue, which runs along the lake shore, Alexander, Cedar and Mandeville lay out a grid of narrow house lots, most of them still vacant. In the lower part Lambert, Van Avenue and Romain Avenue run from Colfax Avenue to Lakeside Avenue, with Lambert Street continuing beyond it; these blocks hold a denser group of frame dwellings, a greenhouse and some small sheds. A large open tract, block 58, fills the middle of the sheet, crossed by a drawn line running from the lake outlet towards Colfax Avenue. Housing elsewhere is thin: scattered frame dwellings along Schuyler, Grant and Colfax Avenues and a few beside the railroad, where one street is marked not named. Water pipes, some proposed, and hydrants are shown, with fire alarm boxes on Colfax and Lakeside Avenues. Block numbers 32 to 60 with older numbers in brackets are printed, and the adjoining sheets 4 and 10 are noted.
notes: Turned on the page; the printed north arrow points about 10 degrees further anticlockwise than the fitted north (magnetic north).
Cedar and Mandeville are printed without suffixes; OpenStreetMap has Cedar Street and Mandeville Street. Alexander is not in OpenStreetMap.
Lambert, west of Lakeside Avenue, does not match modern Lambert Street (its junction was rejected 12 m off); Lambert Street east of Lakeside Avenue does.
N.Y.S.& W. R.R. along the left edge.

Scale 100 ft, sheet turned: north points left (about -75 degrees). Colfax Av, Schuyler Av, Grant Av, Alexander, Cedar, Mandeville, Lakeside Av, Lambert, Van Av, Romain Av; N.Y.S.& W. R.R. along the left; Pompton Lake.

sheet-10-1.description: The western part of sheet 10, at 100 feet to an inch with north up, separated from the turned eastern part by a heavy line that bends around the outlet of Pompton Lake. It covers the residential district east of the town centre from Lakeside Avenue at the top to below Passaic Avenue. In the upper left are the blocks between Romain Avenue, Van Avenue and Lambert, laid out in narrow lots between Lakeside Avenue and Lenox Avenue, with frame dwellings concentrated along Romain Avenue and Romain's Hotel with its boat houses and a garage on the lake shore at the end of Lakeside Avenue. Pompton Lake and its outlet stream run along the dividing line, crossed by a concrete bridge on Lakeside Avenue. South of Lenox Avenue the land is mostly open: Pompton Avenue curves east from Romain Avenue, Summit Avenue runs south-east from it, and Bartholf and Passaic Avenues end at Lincoln Avenue along the left edge, where a row of dwellings faces Lincoln Avenue. Large undivided tracts, numbered 67 and 68, fill the middle of the sheet with only a few scattered houses. Water pipes and hydrants are drawn along Lakeside, Romain, Van and Lincoln Avenues and Pompton and Summit Avenues. Block numbers 65 to 68 with older numbers in brackets are printed, and the adjoining sheets 5, 7, 9 and 11 are noted in the margins.
notes: Romain's Hotel on Lakeside Avenue at the lake.
Lambert, drawn south of Lakeside Avenue between Van Avenue and the lake, is not in OpenStreetMap; Lambert Street meets Lakeside Avenue from the north.

Scale 100 ft, two parts divided by a heavy line. Part 1 (left, north up): Lakeside Av, Lenox Av, Romain Av, Van Av, Lambert, Pompton Av, Summit Av, Bartholf Av, Lincoln Av, Passaic Av. Part 2 (right, turned, north to the upper left): Howard, Poplar (Chestnut), Walnut, Railroad Av, Maple, Dupont Pl, Cannon Ball Rd, Crandall, Circle Av; Dupont Cap Works beyond. Part 2 placed from three hand-picked junctions (the detector found none reliable); fitted north about -63 degrees, the arrow (-70) is magnetic.

sheet-10-2.description: The eastern part of sheet 10, east of a heavy dividing line, drawn at 100 feet to an inch but turned on the page so that north points to the upper left. It shows the workers' housing district beside the Dupont cap works, whose grounds lie beyond the upper edge and are marked as Dupont Cap Works, admittance refused. Howard runs diagonally across the middle of the part with a railroad siding along it, lined on both sides by closely spaced two-family frame dwellings. Poplar (Chestnut), Maple (Dupont) Place and a driveway lead off it, and Walnut, also lettered Railroad Avenue, runs down the right side parallel to the New York, Susquehanna and Western railroad tracks at the right edge, again with rows of dwellings and a hose reel house. Below Howard, Dupont Place leads south-west to Cannon Ball Road, beside a pump house and filter bed of the private water supply. At the bottom, Cannon Ball Road runs down towards the right with Crandall and Circle Avenue branching from it, a street marked not opened, narrow house lots and small dwellings and stores. Much of the land between is open. Block numbers 1, 2, 2A, 2B and 41 to 44 are printed. Water pipes from the Dupont private supply and hydrants are drawn along the streets.
notes: Turned on the page: north is about 63 degrees anticlockwise from up in the fit; the printed north arrow (about 70 degrees) appears to point to magnetic north.
Cannon Ball Road is Cannonball Road in OpenStreetMap; Walnut (Railroad Avenue) is Walnut Street; Howard is Howard Street and Howard Avenue.
Placed from three hand-picked junctions (the detector paired the siding and lot lines); low confidence.
Dupont Cap Works beyond, admittance refused.

Scale 100 ft, two parts divided by a heavy line. Part 1 (left, north up): Lakeside Av, Lenox Av, Romain Av, Van Av, Lambert, Pompton Av, Summit Av, Bartholf Av, Lincoln Av, Passaic Av. Part 2 (right, turned, north to the upper left): Howard, Poplar (Chestnut), Walnut, Railroad Av, Maple, Dupont Pl, Cannon Ball Rd, Crandall, Circle Av; Dupont Cap Works beyond. Part 2 placed from three hand-picked junctions (the detector found none reliable); fitted north about -63 degrees, the arrow (-70) is magnetic.

sheet-11-1.description: The main part of sheet 11, drawn at 100 feet to an inch, covering the south-western residential district of Pompton Lakes between Whitney Avenue and the Paterson and Hamburg Turnpike. In the upper left Whitney Avenue curves around a fan of house lots, with Butler and Center running off it; Ramapo Avenue runs down the middle of the sheet and Lincoln Avenue further east, crossed by Whitney Avenue, Edwin Place, Corning Avenue and Pequannock Avenue. The Paterson and Hamburg Turnpike crosses diagonally from the top centre to the lower right, with Mountain Avenue leaving it to the east, and Mill Street, marked not opened in part, runs along the bottom edge. The district is almost wholly residential: frame dwellings with garages on narrow lots, densest along Ramapo Avenue and the turnpike, with many lots still vacant and large undivided tracts in the east. A few non-residential buildings stand out: an auto repair shop at the top beside the turnpike, a printing and dyeing works building west of Ramapo Avenue, apartments, and the New Paradise Inn standing alone at the right edge, with a small store or garage near the bottom right corner. Water pipes of four and six inches and hydrants are drawn in the streets, with fire alarm boxes on Whitney and Ramapo Avenues. Block numbers 80 to 94 with suffixes and older numbers in brackets are printed, and the adjoining sheets 6, 7, 10 and 1 are noted in the margins. The lower left corner is taken up by an inset, boxed off by a heavy line, which is a separate part.
notes: The Paterson & Hamburg Turnpike (Paterson-Hamburg Turnpike in OpenStreetMap) was left out of the control: its junctions on this sheet were 4 to 7 m off a fit to the other streets, and dropping it took the fit from 3.7 to 1.0 m RMSE; the modern road appears widened or realigned.
Butler and Center are printed without a suffix; OpenStreetMap has Butler Street and Center Street.
New Paradise Inn at the right edge.

Scale 100 ft, two parts. Part 1 (main): Whitney Av, Butler, Center, Ramapo Av, Edwin Pl, Lincoln Av, Mountain Av, Paterson & Hamburg Tpke, Corning Av, Pequannock Av, Mill St. Part 2: inset lower left behind a heavy line, Ringwood Av and Paterson & Hamburg Tpke with the Pompton Reformed Church and cemetery. Paterson-Hamburg Turnpike left out of part 1's control (junctions 4 to 7 m off). Part 2 anchored on Ringwood Av / Tpke.

sheet-11-2.description: An inset in the lower left corner of sheet 11, boxed off by a heavy line, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with its own north arrow pointing up. It shows an area west of the main map, on the Paterson and Hamburg Turnpike, which runs along the bottom of the inset, at its junction with Ringwood Avenue, which runs north from it. West of Ringwood Avenue is the Pompton Reformed Church, a frame church with a spire, steam heat and electric lights, with its Sunday school building beside it, set at the southern end of a large cemetery that fills most of the left half of the inset. East of Ringwood Avenue lie two blocks of house lots with frame dwellings, a building of apartments and garages facing Ringwood Avenue, and a large open block further north. A six inch water pipe runs along Ringwood Avenue and the turnpike, with a hydrant and a fire alarm box at the corner. Block numbers 28 to 30 with older numbers in brackets are printed, and the note no exposure beyond runs along the bottom edge.
notes: Pompton Reformed Church and Sunday School beside the cemetery.
Placed from the single junction of Ringwood Avenue and the turnpike, with the scale of the main map and the rotation of the drawn street lines; low confidence.

Scale 100 ft, two parts. Part 1 (main): Whitney Av, Butler, Center, Ramapo Av, Edwin Pl, Lincoln Av, Mountain Av, Paterson & Hamburg Tpke, Corning Av, Pequannock Av, Mill St. Part 2: inset lower left behind a heavy line, Ringwood Av and Paterson & Hamburg Tpke with the Pompton Reformed Church and cemetery. Paterson-Hamburg Turnpike left out of part 1's control (junctions 4 to 7 m off). Part 2 anchored on Ringwood Av / Tpke.
